subject: BibTeX and links for papers on web site

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: BibTeX and links for papers on web site
parts:
Michael and I have had a whack at redesigning the
web site. The latest version is in the repo
webpages under mc-stan.org/index.html.

Right now, we have BibTeX for the papers.

Two questions:

1. move to just a bibliography-style citation and
don't be so complete, and

2. include links?

We'll keep the BibTeX for the links we suggest for
referring to Stan.

Pro and con for 1 are obvious.

Pro for 2 is that it's more incentive to actually look
at the papers. Con is that links rot and are harder to
include in the first place.

My own experience trying to do this over two decades is
that links always rot. Things are much better now than 10
years ago. Responsible sites will redirect, but journals
get sold, consolidated, move to JSTOR, etc. (This was
part of the motivation for the DOI system, but it hasn't
been widely accepted outside of bio.)

The question to me is whether the live links make up for
us having to create them, and then either check them or
let them go dead.

- Bob
